Same camera, room width, wall corners, ceiling, tall Bosch refrigerator with bottom freezer drawer, Wolf/hood/pot filler, SMEG, cabinets/lights, concrete floor, both countertops. The projecting cabinet tower on the LEFT is COMPLETELY WRONG. REMOVE the ENTIRE tower: all side panels, plinth, legs, projecting worktop, coffee cupboard, wood-lined spice/electronics shelves. REMOVE the Italy poster and frame entirely. Restore the original FLAT plaster WALL PLANE and floor where the tower projected. No ledge, boxed-out column, cabinet top or freestanding furniture remains.
In that same ORIGINAL wall plane, embed two separate elegant FLUSH openings on one vertical centerline. Lower: a compact15-inch-class wine refrigerator, black tinted glass face with restrained thin brushed-metal edge, discreet recessed pull and visible warm-lit wine racks. Its CLOSED door/front is COPLANAR WITH THE PLASTER WALL, not projecting. The appliance body is NOT visible; no side depth, no countertop over it, no raised surround. A slim ventilation strip at its bottom also sits in the wall plane. Upper: a refined approximately18-inch-wide white COFFEE-GARAGE panel, completely CLOSED and FLUSH WITH THE SAME WALL, matching wall color, precise tiny shadow gap and discreet touch-latch edge. Behind it is the compact espresso machine on a pull-out tray, but NOTHING protrudes or is visible while closed. Leave a calm band of ordinary plaster wall between the wine face and coffee panel. No continuous tall cabinet carcass; the wall itself remains uninterrupted around the two separate flush faces.
No spices, smart speaker, phone, charging dock or artwork anywhere on this end wall. Those belong on the OTHER sink-side wall and are OUT OF VIEW here. Counter above dishwasher at extremeleft stays completely clear. Do not change main fridge, add room depth or widen floor/aisle. Refined minimalist integrated detailing, existing warm palette and real texture. The absence of projection is critical: WALL-FLUSH BOTH wine and closed coffee front. One photoreal16:9 image, no labels/diagrams.
